app.title: Exoplanet Data Visualization
app.summary: The catalogue of planet candidates loads when the app starts. The live API is tried first, and a bundled CSV is used if the API fails. Each planet is binned by host-star size and given a habitability status from its temperature and gravity classes. The person narrows the catalogue by a planet-radius range and a choice of star-size classes, then presses Apply. Four charts redraw: temperature against orbital distance, position on the sky, distribution of distance relative to stellar radius, and star mass against star temperature. A paged table of the filtered rows also redraws. A field dictionary explains each column.

task.text: Explore a planet-candidate catalogue by filtering on planet radius and host-star size and seeing how the remaining planets' habitability classes spread across orbital, sky and stellar properties.

data.text: A catalogue table of planet candidates with orbital, planetary and host-star properties, plus derived classes for star size, temperature, gravity and habitability status.
data.item: a planet candidate with its host star's properties

stage.text: exploring a published planet-candidate catalogue, before choosing targets for closer study

mechanism.text: A radius range slider and a star-size multi-select are applied together with a button. The filtered rows go into a store that redraws four scatter and histogram charts, coloured by star size or habitability status, plus a paged raw table in a separate tab.

field.text: exoplanet catalogue exploration and habitability screening in astronomy

workflow.name: filter a catalogue and see the remaining items across several charts

steps.here: At startup the app fetches the catalogue from the Asterank Kepler API and falls back to a bundled CSV. It drops rows with no period or missing radius or temperature.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each planet is binned into small, similar or bigger star size and into temperature and gravity classes. Those classes give it a promising, challenging or extreme status. Orbital distance divided by stellar radius gives a relative distance.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: A range slider sets the planet-radius range and a multi-select dropdown picks star-size classes. Apply stores the filtered rows.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Four charts redraw from the filtered rows. Temperature vs distance is coloured by star size. The sky position and star mass vs temperature scatters are sized by planet radius and coloured by status. A relative-distance histogram has an Earth marker at 1.
The Data tab shows the filtered rows' original columns in a paged table of 40 rows per page. The About tab gives a dictionary of every field.

distinctive: A rule-based habitability status combines a temperature class and a gravity class (from radius) into promising, challenging or extreme
Planets are grouped by host-star size relative to the Sun (below 0.8, 0.8–1.2, above 1.2 solar radii)
A relative-distance histogram (orbital distance divided by stellar radius) marks Earth's position at 1
Sky position is plotted from right ascension and declination, with point size showing planet radius
Live API fetch, with a bundled CSV as a fallback
